text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Tuesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas accepted the resignation of Finance Minister Rolandas Matiliauskas. Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius said he will choose a new candidate during the next few days.
- Julius Abromavicius, killed in a car explosion on Friday, sent a fax to the prosecutor's office two days before his death naming the people suspected of blowing up a railway bridge in 1994.
- Latvia rejected the invitation of the Lithuanian foreign ministry to restart talks over their disputed sea border.
- After two weeks of negotiations, the government and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) failed to agree on import tariffs but decided to scrap gradually the currency board.
- Central bank officials denied that a secret memorandum with the IMF was drawn up on liquidating the problem struck Innovation bank.
- There are 158 students per 10,000 inhabitants in Lithuania
. - No bank shares saw gains on the bourse on Monday, showing that their prices have stabilised and are too high to attract investors, dealers said.
- Central bank governor Reinoldijus Sharkinas denies a report that the bank will end abruptly the currency board.
- State security officials seized 50 tonnes of contraband high proof spirit which was smuggled from Belarus.
- Vagnorius will talk about obstacles to a free trade agreement in agricultural products during a meeting in Tallin with his Latvian and Estonian counterparts on Thursday.
- The central bank denied a news agency report that a 25 percent devaluation of the litas is inevitable.
- Experts forecast that the share capital of the oil concern Lietuvos Nafta will be 787 million litas, which may be boosted to 1.2 billion litas later on.
